subject: AI & Agents
title: The Energy Cost of AI
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Energy Cost of AI.

hook.text: Training one large AI model can emit as much carbon as five cars over their lifetimes.

buildup.text: AI runs on GPUs in massive data centers that consume electricity around the clock.

discovery.text: GPT-3's training used 1,287 MWh of energy — enough to power 120 US homes for a year.

twist.text: Every AI query you send uses 10x more energy than a Google search.

climax.text: Researchers are developing smaller, efficient models — but the arms race keeps scaling up.

quiz.question: Why is AI training energy-intensive?
options: It requires massive GPU computation over long periods
AI hardware uses solar power only
Models are trained on paper first

details.summary: Training large AI models requires enormous energy — a single GPT-4 training run consumes electricity equivalent to thousands of homes for a year. The environmental cost of AI is often hidden but significant.
details.whyItMatters: As AI scales, its energy footprint grows. Awareness drives demand for efficient models, renewable-powered data centers, and honest accounting of AI's environmental impact.
takeaways: Training large models consumes megawatt-hours of electricity
AI's carbon footprint is growing rapidly with model scale
Efficiency improvements and renewable energy are critical responses

faq.question: How much energy does AI actually use?
faq.answer: Training a large language model can use hundreds of megawatt-hours. AI data centers globally consume an estimated 1-2% of world electricity, a figure projected to grow significantly as AI adoption accelerates.

faq.question: What can be done about AI's energy consumption?
faq.answer: Smaller efficient models, improved hardware, renewable energy for data centers, and quantization techniques that reduce computation all help. Choosing appropriately sized models for each task also reduces waste.
